clusters.name: Persistence and Data Access Pattern
clusters.description: Architectural choices for storing and retrieving bike and usage data, distinct from presentation, workflow, security, and live-update concerns.

relations.rationale: Operational dashboards and usage analytics require a defined mechanism for retrieving persisted bike and usage records.

values.label: Repository-Based Persistence
values.description: Encapsulates persistence operations behind repositories so business logic remains independent of storage technology.

values.label: Repository-Based Analytics Queries
values.description: Uses repository abstractions to query usage statistics and other analytics-oriented records.

clusters.name: Operational Monitoring and Analytics
clusters.description: Choices for aggregating, presenting, and interpreting operational bike status and usage information, separate from underlying persistence and event delivery.

relations.rationale: Monitoring and analytics depend on access to persisted bike and usage data, regardless of the chosen dashboard technology.
Live status broadcasting supplies monitoring dashboards with current bike-state information.

values.label: Real-Time Bike Status Dashboard

values.label: Usage Analytics Dashboard
values.description: Aggregates and analyzes usage data to support operational reporting and platform insight.

clusters.name: Verification Challenge Design
clusters.description: Choices governing verification challenges, credential delivery, validity windows, and delivery feedback, distinct from authenticated-session controls.

values.label: Thirty-Minute Verification Code
values.description: Issues verification codes that remain valid for thirty minutes before expiration.

values.label: Thirty-Second Verification Code
values.description: Issues short-lived verification codes with a thirty-second validity window to reduce reuse and interception risk.

values.label: Customer Verification-Code Delivery
values.description: Delivers verification codes to customers and reports successful delivery within the verification workflow.

clusters.name: Authenticated Session Protection
clusters.description: Choices for protecting already authenticated user sessions through inactivity handling, distinct from initial identity verification and rental workflow control.

values.label: Inactivity-Based Session Timeout
values.description: Automatically logs users out after fifteen minutes of inactivity to limit exposure from unattended sessions.

clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle Control
clusters.description: Choices for representing and controlling the progression of a bike rental, including navigation, unlocking, duration, expiry, and notifications.

relations.rationale: Rental state transitions can generate bike-status changes that must be distributed to dashboards and monitoring consumers.

values.label: State-Machine Rental Workflow
values.description: Models navigation, QR scanning, unlocking, and rental progression as explicit state transitions.

values.label: Duration-Aware Rental Scheduling
values.description: Tracks elapsed rental duration and manages time-based rental controls.

values.label: Pre-Expiry Rental Alerts
values.description: Notifies riders before a rental reaches its expiry or approaching end.

clusters.name: Real-Time Status Distribution

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The minibatch repeats concepts already captured by the current dimensions: real-time bike status monitoring and usage analytics map to Operational Monitoring and Analytics; repository pattern, bike data persistence abstraction, and usage statistics querying via repository map to Persistence and Data Access Pattern; time-limited verification code issuance and delivery/feedback map to Verification Challenge Design; inactivity-based session timeout maps to Authenticated Session Protection; rental lifecycle management, navigation, QR scan/unlock transition, duration tracking, pre-expiry notifications, and time-based rental control map to Rental Lifecycle Control; and observer-based real-time status broadcasting with dashboard/monitoring subscribers maps to Real-Time Status Distribution. No open code introduces a new architectural concern that cannot be absorbed by an existing axis of variation for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. Payment provider API abstraction, common payment interfaces, and pluggable payment methods fit Dimension 7 (Payment Integration Strategy). End-to-end encryption, encrypted storage of registration data, privacy-focused handling, protected credential transmission, and protected credential storage fit Dimension 8 (Data Security and Privacy Controls). Event-driven registration workflow and downstream bike removal/state update fit Dimension 6 (Real-Time Status and Event Distribution), while the rental lifecycle/state-machine and command-based encapsulation of rental operations, plus separated notification scheduling, fit Dimension 5 (Rental Lifecycle and Operation Control). The report-related codes align with Dimension 9 (Report Construction and Export), and email-password authentication fits Dimension 3 (Identity Verification and Authentication). No open code introduces a new architectural axis distinct from the existing dimensions for the CityBike use case.
